Die junge Anwältin Mia Stocker tritt ihre erste Arbeitsstelle in der renommierten Kanzlei ihres Vaters an. Ihr erster Fall scheint reine Routine zu sein: In einem Pflegeheim stirbt ein alter Herr an einer falschen Medikation. Mia vertritt den Betreiber des Pflegeheims. Zusammen mit ihrem ehrgeizigen Kollegen Jan Wilke gelingt es, die Schuld auf die Pflegerin Dana abzuwälzen. Doch als Dana in der Haft ums Leben kommt, spürt Mia, dass mehr hinter dem vermeintlich klaren Fall steckt.

Der Fernsehturm ist das Wahrzeichen Berlins - der Höhepunkt der Skyline und von überall zu sehen. Mit seinen 368 Metern ist er nicht nur das höchste Gebäude Deutschlands, sondern auch ein Symbol für den Wandel der Stadt.

In keinem anderen Land sind die Saisonunterschiede so groß wie hier. Vor allem der Winter erfordert besondere Vorbereitung. Riesige Gebirge, das Land umschließende Ozeane und die nördliche Lage erwecken einen der härtesten Winter der Erde. Vorbereitung ist alles, wenn sich die kalte Jahreszeit ankündigt - das Land friert ein, Stürme wüten, und eine endlose Dunkelheit umfasst das Land.
Die Reihe widmet sich dem Brauchtum, der Geschichte, der Wirtschaft, dem Lifestyle und der Kulinarik unserer Nachbarländer.

pr.t: Brahmaputra - Der große Fluss vom Himalaya
pr.d: Der Brahmaputra legt von seiner Quelle am Dach der Welt bis zur Mündung im Indischen Ozean rund 3.100 Kilometer zurück. Er ernährt Millionen von Menschen in China, Indien und Bangladesch und erschafft riesige Gebiete voll faszinierender Biodiversität. Brahmaputra, Sohn des Schöpfers, ist nur einer seiner vielen Namen. Im Oberlauf, im Tibetischen Hochland, heißt er Yarlung Tsangpo. Er erzählt die turbulente Geschichte eines gigantischen Gebirges und eines ebenso stattlichen Flusses.

Sie sind Zeugen jener Zeit, in der gummibereifte Räder laufen lernten, die Kolben der Motoren auf und ab stampften, der Treibstoff in der Apotheke zu beziehen war: die Oldtimer. Damals war sportliches Autofahren noch einer Mutprobe gleichzusetzen. Oliver Zeisberger hat verschiedenste Autos in der atemberaubenden Bergwelt der Obersteiermark gefilmt, in Szene gesetzt und versucht, deren Geschichten zu erfahren.

pr.d: Zwischen Quelle und Schlucht und entlang des Hauptkamms des Himalaya erschließt sich die wohl dynamischste Landschaft der Erde. Die tiefsten und längsten Schluchten der Welt verbinden die Welten, die das höchste Gebirge der Erde trennt.

pr.t: Brahmaputra - Der große Fluss vom Himalaya
pr.d: Der Oberlauf des Brahmaputra, der indische Yarlung Tsangpo fließt von seinem Ursprung in 5.200 Meter Höhe 1.700 Kilometer westwärts, bis der Namjagbarwa ihn in eine riesige Schleife und dann in die tiefste und längste Schlucht der Welt zwingt.
In der Sendung werden Geschichten von Menschen gezeigt, die kulinarisch etwas zu bieten haben.

In der Sendung wird im Winter vom Skifahren und Skitourengehen und im Sommer vom Bergwandern und Bergsteigen berichtet. Das Programm ist nicht nur für Spezialisten, sondern soll ein breites Spektrum an Bergfreunden erreichen.

Über Jahrhunderte war Walfang ein lukrativer Wirtschaftszweig. Heute riskieren Walretter für jedes einzelne Tier, wenn nötig ihr Leben. Vor knapp 50 Jahren veröffentlichte der US-Biologe Roger Payne eine Schallplatte mit den Gesängen von Buckelwalen.

Die Weihnachtsinsel ist nur ein kleiner Punkt im Indischen Ozean. Ihre paradiesische Kulisse ist die Bühne für ein besonderes Tier: bis zu einem Meter groß und an die 100 Jahre alt. Es knackt Kokosnüsse und zieht den Menschen das Essen vom Teller.

In den Tiefen der Meere lebt eine Gruppe von Tieren mit unglaublichen Fähigkeiten. Knochenlose Kreaturen, die Farbe und Form verändern können. Saugnäpfe machen sie zu effizienten Jägern: Tintenfische. Ihnen wird auf den Grund gegangen.

In den Weiten des Südpazifiks liegt die Republik Fidschi. Die meisten der 300 Fidschi-Inseln sind verwitterte Spitzen erloschener Vulkane. Der Film spürt dem Leben der Menschen auf Fidschi nach und führt in eine faszinierende Inselwelt im Südpazifik.

Die erfolgreichste Freitaucherin Anna von Bötticher besucht Regionen, die vom Wasser geprägt sind. Sie unternimmt Tauchgänge und zeigt, was Wasser an verschiedenen Orten der Erde bedeutet und wie Menschen mit dem Wasser leben.

Few have ever heard about the ultra top-secret military base in the remote deserts of Utah known as Area 52.

A man with a late-night urge to relieve himself picks an unusual spot to go; a fugitive leads police on a wild foot chase down the middle of a busy motorway; a woman involved in a fender bender has an over-the-top reaction.
A naked man makes a scene on a Miami Beach, a drunk driver finds a strange and dangerous place to relieve himself, and the mayor of a Minnesota town finds himself in police custody.
Auctions in Garland bring a day of dashed hopes and sweet profits. Plus, a new buyer begins to throw some of the bidders off their game.
A local auctioneer stirs up things when the buyers return to Fort Worth, Jenny and Mary disagree on the value of their purchases and Victor's protégé stands to lose the most.
The sibling rivalry between Seth and Ashley is at an all-time high and when Ashley faces down not one, but two baseball deals that are clearly outside her comfort zone, Seth cries foul.
Brawling isn't exactly out of the ordinary at American Jewelry and Loan, but when customers start throwing down in the car park before the doors even open, Les knows it's a bad sign.

With Les out of commission, Seth and Ashley run the shop as co-managers, but when Seth's decision to cut back on staff leaves Ashley alone on the floor with one too many crazy customers, it's clear that sharing duties just won't work.

David Dickinson helps the people of Carlisle sort the treasures from their rubbish. Antiques dealers Debbie Serpell, Helen Gardiner, Stewart Hofgartner and Tim Hogarth are on hand, with an art deco tea set that really catches the eye.

David and the team are in Blackburn where they come face to face with a tiger, other items of interest include a Doulton facemask which Corrie Jeffrey worries she has been charmed by, and Mark Stevens meets his match when he haggles with a father and son over a gentleman's wristwatch.
When Rick gets his hands on a pretty stellar coin, Corey flips about the astronomical asking price. Next, Chum goes to the mat when an NWA Championship Wrestling Belt elbows its way into the shop.

Scott and Sheldon venture into cowboy country, meeting a collector of 40s-60s cowboy movie and TV memorabilia. Later, they discover a celebrity pilot's two hangars full of old planes, cars, and bikes.
The guys pick a Pennsylvania warehouse and find a rare comic book, Frank tries to negotiate for a vintage cigarette machine, a ramshackle old house is said to be haunted by a ghost named Pearl.
Picking Superheroes: Mike and Frank find a rare comic book in an old Pennsylvanian warehouse. They also pick a spine-tingling home haunted by a ghost named Pearl. (S5, ep 13)

A Chilean family might have photographed a real UFO flying above the Andes Mountains. Footage of a tall, dark-coloured, hairy creature walking through the woods could prove the legendary Ohio Grassman exists.

A loyal viewer might have captured an image of an alien probe. The identity of a bizarre creature spotted on a driveway camera. The legendary Men in Black might have called a man and threatened him. A family survived a bolt of lightning.

A silver orb in the sky, and alleged crash debris may be from a UFO. A 65-year-old-man might have some of the fastest hands in the West. An infamous spy organisation's alleged footage of UFOs and aliens.

A photograph of a UFO hovering over Holloman Air Force Base in New Mexico, a cabin built in a supposedly anomalous spot that defies gravity in the Redwood Forests, the origin of frightening howls recorded in Witset, British Columbia.
Chum chases down a lead on a 1963 Fiat Microcar. Next, Jake gets a lesson from big brother Corey when a rare musical instrument enters the shop. Rick and Corey disagree on a set of billiard balls.
Englishman David Kay joins the auction action in Fort Worth, Victor uncovers spy gear, Ricky and Bubba try to land something large and dangerous.
The bidders compete in Dallas, Lesa and Jerry pester Mary and Jenny, cowboy Matt Blevins is targeted by Ricky and Bubba, a musical instrument's fate garners differing opinions.

Ivy drags Isaiah to Victorville as punishment for getting C's on his report card. Kenny wants to furnish his new house, but there are eight reasons standing in his way. And not to be cheesy, but Lisa learns a lot.
Brandi is fired up about expanding her brand in San Bernardino. Rene is positive that everyone is out to get him. Dusty tackles a locker dustier than him. Kenny is a mess.

From ancient sites like Stonehenge to the crop circle phenomenon and modern-day UFO sightings, Great Britain is a place of mysteries; exploring if throughout history this island has been a destination for extraterrestrial visitors.

Britain's sharpest armchair critics share more of their sharp, insightful, passionate and sometimes emotional critiques of the week's biggest and best shows on television.

pr.t: Gordon Ramsay's 24 Hours to Hell and Back
pr.d: At Brownstone Bistro in Los Angeles, Gordon has just 24 hours to give the restaurant a vibrant new look and introduce a simplified menu featuring fresh and authentic Caribbean fare in a highly competitive culinary scene.
Offering their unmatched satirical insight into current world events, Adam, Josh and Alex are joined by Harriet Dyer and Josh Pugh to help dissect the biggest news stories of the week.

pr.t: AI: Probably Nothing to Worry About
pr.d: The fullest account yet of AI's origins, told by the people who built it. Not just a tech history lesson but an anarchic thriller, this is the story of a technology whose power isn't in the algorithms, but in the handful of people who control it.

In the west of Scotland, Gavin and Johanna start things off with a loosely Italian-themed menu. Day two sees Sharyn and David's main course of beef stroganoff failing to live up to its billing. Finally, Daljit and Gordon get their turn to impress.

pr.t: Kirstie and Phil's Love It or List It
pr.d: Kirstie and Phil head to Nottingham, where Lexie and Ed are at a stalemate. Their four-bed, one-bathroom home is fit to burst, and Ed just wants to pack up and move to a bigger house. But Lexie thinks, with Kirstie's help, that the house could work.

Eddie becomes an ice skater in a penguin suit for ice shows and invites Carla to see the show in Seattle. She is reluctant to go to Seattle. At first, she seems ashamed of Eddie's current job, but she later admits that she is afraid of flying.
Rebecca is filled with jealousy when Evan Drake promotes Sam to an executive sales job at corporate headquarters. After some thought, she starts to suspect there are ulterior motives.
Financial problems mean Doug's bowling team must either win their next game or lose their sponsor. Doug soon realises Carrie is the problem so he removes her from the team.
Doug reluctantly agrees to invest his Christmas bonus in an online business., and Arthur tries to outdo the neighbours' big wreath.
Doug's cousin Danny has no best man for his marriage, so Doug reluctantly fills in and arranges a bachelor party. Unfortunately Danny doesn't seem to have many friends who want to come.
Ray and Debra vow to change their ways when they realise they're nicer to strangers than each other, and Ray's friend Doug has to visit the doctor after he's hit by a foul ball at a Mets game.
Ray urges Debra to go dancing with Robert, but then he starts to think it's something more and becomes increasingly jealous.
After everyone sees Robert and Amy having sex, they move into Ray's basement office to enjoy some privacy.
Frasier gives both Daphne and Niles romantic advice; Daphne's demanding mother and deadbeat brother complicate her wedding.
Niles and Daphne discover that there is a heavy price to pay for admitting their true love. Among those ranged against the lovers are Daphne's jilted groom Donny and Niles' bitter wife Mel.
Frasier convinces his father to visit an old person's home so that he can meet the beautiful female boss. Frasier's plan does not work out when he discovers that his father actually likes the home.

pr.t: Gordon Ramsay's 24 Hours to Hell and Back
pr.d: Gordon visits M'Dears Bakery and Bistro in Los Angeles, which specialises in Southern cuisine with a Californian twist, to revamp the dated dining area and the menu.
Channel 4's midday news summary.

In Cornwall, interior designer Anouska and Greig create a basement cinema room. Rosi and Antony attempt to transport 300 tonnes of salvaged items to their Scottish farmhouse. And in Shropshire, Catherine meets a very special former resident.

Seán gets into deep water with his Apollo Beach fishing charter business. In Miami, Charmaine is running a multi-million-pound business from her bedroom while homeschooling her daughter. And Gary and Maria are expecting more grandchildren.
Colin Murray, Rachel Riley and Susie Dent host, with Konnie Huq in Dictionary Corner, as contestants race against the clock to pit their wits against vowels, consonants and numbers.

Ben Hillman house-hunts with retired couple Clare and Alan around the central Algarve region in Portugal. The couple are dreaming of a three-bed holiday home where they can spend plenty of time with their family.

Francesca and Carl have committed to bringing two abandoned Italian villages back to life. Meanwhile, tricky climate conditions lead to a worrying olive harvest at Lucie and Jerry's borgo. In France, it's opening time at Kevin and Anna's new pub.

Karen and Adrian stake a claim for being the busiest B&Bers in 'Four in a Bed' history at The Barn in North Yorkshire. One guest reckons that such a big to-do list means the hosts haven't paid enough attention to his poached eggs at breakfast.

Former-beauty-queen-turned-property-developer Joey hosts the third night in north Wales. She's hoping her pageant-themed evening and glam food will wow her guests and win her another crown and the £1000 prize.

Wendy and Andrew want to buy a holiday home in the whitewashed villages of Andalucía. Craig Rowe shows them five options for their maximum budget of £217k, from a traditional place that has them beaming to a townhouse that they've already viewed.
A special edition of Channel 4's flagship news programme, including the weather.

Lebanese journalist Janay Boulos and Syrian filmmaker Abd Alkader Habak collaborate remotely from thousands of miles apart. With both their homelands ravaged by war, what threatens to tear them apart ultimately brings them closer together.
We catch up with Cara and Ben in Essex, who found their dream digs in 2016. And after a successful search in 2014, how are Sally and Steve getting on in their Warwickshire abode?
As public attention intensifies, the women find themselves living under an increasingly unforgiving spotlight. And one question becomes impossible to ignore: is Alice Bell hiding in plain sight?

Father and son duo Brian and Thomas visit the First Dates restaurant for a double date. A make-up influencer struggles to open up to his tall, dark and handsome date. And a disco dancing widower seeks more than just a dance partner as he turns 60.

It's the semi-final and time for the bakers to showcase their patisserie prowess. Their precision, patience and pastry skills are pushed to the limit as they strive to prove they have what it takes to make it through to the final.

pr.t: The Great British Bake Off: Second Helpings [NEW]
pr.d: Jon Richardson and Judi Love welcome celeb guests to Patisserie Week.

Britain's sharpest armchair critics share more of their sharp, insightful, passionate and sometimes emotional critiques of the week's biggest and best shows on television.

pr.t: Gordon Ramsay's 24 Hours to Hell and Back
pr.d: At Brownstone Bistro in Los Angeles, Gordon has just 24 hours to give the restaurant a vibrant new look and introduce a simplified menu featuring fresh and authentic Caribbean fare in a highly competitive culinary scene.
Offering their unmatched satirical insight into current world events, Adam, Josh and Alex are joined by Harriet Dyer and Josh Pugh to help dissect the biggest news stories of the week.

pr.t: AI: Probably Nothing to Worry About
pr.d: The fullest account yet of AI's origins, told by the people who built it. Not just a tech history lesson but an anarchic thriller, this is the story of a technology whose power isn't in the algorithms, but in the handful of people who control it.

In the west of Scotland, Gavin and Johanna start things off with a loosely Italian-themed menu. Day two sees Sharyn and David's main course of beef stroganoff failing to live up to its billing. Finally, Daljit and Gordon get their turn to impress.

pr.t: Kirstie and Phil's Love It or List It
pr.d: Kirstie and Phil head to Nottingham, where Lexie and Ed are at a stalemate. Their four-bed, one-bathroom home is fit to burst, and Ed just wants to pack up and move to a bigger house. But Lexie thinks, with Kirstie's help, that the house could work.

Eddie becomes an ice skater in a penguin suit for ice shows and invites Carla to see the show in Seattle. She is reluctant to go to Seattle. At first, she seems ashamed of Eddie's current job, but she later admits that she is afraid of flying.
Rebecca is filled with jealousy when Evan Drake promotes Sam to an executive sales job at corporate headquarters. After some thought, she starts to suspect there are ulterior motives.
Financial problems mean Doug's bowling team must either win their next game or lose their sponsor. Doug soon realises Carrie is the problem so he removes her from the team.
Doug reluctantly agrees to invest his Christmas bonus in an online business., and Arthur tries to outdo the neighbours' big wreath.
Doug's cousin Danny has no best man for his marriage, so Doug reluctantly fills in and arranges a bachelor party. Unfortunately Danny doesn't seem to have many friends who want to come.
Ray and Debra vow to change their ways when they realise they're nicer to strangers than each other, and Ray's friend Doug has to visit the doctor after he's hit by a foul ball at a Mets game.
Ray urges Debra to go dancing with Robert, but then he starts to think it's something more and becomes increasingly jealous.
After everyone sees Robert and Amy having sex, they move into Ray's basement office to enjoy some privacy.
Frasier gives both Daphne and Niles romantic advice; Daphne's demanding mother and deadbeat brother complicate her wedding.
Niles and Daphne discover that there is a heavy price to pay for admitting their true love. Among those ranged against the lovers are Daphne's jilted groom Donny and Niles' bitter wife Mel.
Frasier convinces his father to visit an old person's home so that he can meet the beautiful female boss. Frasier's plan does not work out when he discovers that his father actually likes the home.

pr.t: Gordon Ramsay's 24 Hours to Hell and Back
pr.d: Gordon visits M'Dears Bakery and Bistro in Los Angeles, which specialises in Southern cuisine with a Californian twist, to revamp the dated dining area and the menu.
Channel 4's midday news summary.

In Cornwall, interior designer Anouska and Greig create a basement cinema room. Rosi and Antony attempt to transport 300 tonnes of salvaged items to their Scottish farmhouse. And in Shropshire, Catherine meets a very special former resident.

Seán gets into deep water with his Apollo Beach fishing charter business. In Miami, Charmaine is running a multi-million-pound business from her bedroom while homeschooling her daughter. And Gary and Maria are expecting more grandchildren.
Colin Murray, Rachel Riley and Susie Dent host, with Konnie Huq in Dictionary Corner, as contestants race against the clock to pit their wits against vowels, consonants and numbers.

Ben Hillman house-hunts with retired couple Clare and Alan around the central Algarve region in Portugal. The couple are dreaming of a three-bed holiday home where they can spend plenty of time with their family.

Francesca and Carl have committed to bringing two abandoned Italian villages back to life. Meanwhile, tricky climate conditions lead to a worrying olive harvest at Lucie and Jerry's borgo. In France, it's opening time at Kevin and Anna's new pub.

Karen and Adrian stake a claim for being the busiest B&Bers in 'Four in a Bed' history at The Barn in North Yorkshire. One guest reckons that such a big to-do list means the hosts haven't paid enough attention to his poached eggs at breakfast.

Former-beauty-queen-turned-property-developer Joey hosts the third night in north Wales. She's hoping her pageant-themed evening and glam food will wow her guests and win her another crown and the £1000 prize.

Wendy and Andrew want to buy a holiday home in the whitewashed villages of Andalucía. Craig Rowe shows them five options for their maximum budget of £217k, from a traditional place that has them beaming to a townhouse that they've already viewed.
A special edition of Channel 4's flagship news programme, including the weather.

Lebanese journalist Janay Boulos and Syrian filmmaker Abd Alkader Habak collaborate remotely from thousands of miles apart. With both their homelands ravaged by war, what threatens to tear them apart ultimately brings them closer together.

As public attention intensifies, the women find themselves living under an increasingly unforgiving spotlight. And one question becomes impossible to ignore: is Alice Bell hiding in plain sight?

Father and son duo Brian and Thomas visit the First Dates restaurant for a double date. A make-up influencer struggles to open up to his tall, dark and handsome date. And a disco dancing widower seeks more than just a dance partner as he turns 60.

It's the semi-final and time for the bakers to showcase their patisserie prowess. Their precision, patience and pastry skills are pushed to the limit as they strive to prove they have what it takes to make it through to the final.

Duke, an old crony of Salem's and former con man, has finished his sentence as a cat and is ready to go straight, but his commitment soon starts to waver.

Dreama is accidentally turned into a mouse when she catches Sabrina's (Melissa Joan Hart) spring fever.
Joey encounters problems trying to get off the movie set to officiate the wedding when the star turns up drunk.

Monica and Chandler's wedding reception is almost upstaged by the news that someone might be pregnant. Meanwhile, Ross tries to impress a pretty single woman, Chandler has troubles on the dance floor, and Joey hopes to impress Chandler's mum's date, an important Broadway producer, with his acting ability.
The girls speculate as to who's the father of Rachel's baby, the guys scramble after Chandler loses the film from his wedding, and Monica wants to open the wedding gifts.
Everybody seems to know who the father of Rachel's baby is except the man himself. Meanwhile, Phoebe and Joey lie about a gas leak to get into Monica and Chandler's apartment.
Ross gets upset when Rachel goes out on a date with a handsome actor, Phoebe tries to prevent a chef from being sacked, and Chandler kills a co-worker's promotion.
At Monica's Halloween party, Phoebe meets the friendly fiancé of her flighty twin Ursula, but becomes alarmed when she learns that her sister has misrepresented herself to her trusting future in-law.

Feeling guilty for denying Chandler a bachelor party, Monica hires a stripper to perform for him, without learning that she's a prostitute. Elsewhere, Rachel's father learns about her pregnancy and plans to give Ross a piece of his mind.

An old high-school friend of Monica's is invited to the Thanksgiving dinner with the gang, but Monica is unaware that he isn't exactly fond of Rachel. Meanwhile, Chandler and Phoebe pretend to be mesmerised by American football in order to avoid helping Monica in the kitchen, and Joey vows to devour the entire turkey single-handedly.
Chandler is aghast when Monica buys painfully expensive boots, and Phoebe tries to capitalise on her discovery that Ross's son attends school with the son of rock star Sting.
Ross's new girlfriend wants to put their photograph on Christmas cards, Rachel eyes Joey as a possible romantic partner, and the newlyweds cope with Chandler's boss as he goes through a divorce.

As Joey agonises over his secret affection for Rachel, Monica mistakenly thinks that he is infatuated with Phoebe. Meanwhile, Ross and Rachel promise not to try to find out the sex of their unborn child, but Rachel can't resist having a peek inside the doctor's confidential folder. Also, Monica urges a reluctant Chandler to enjoy the soothing pleasures of a scented bath, but realises that she's created a tub monster.

Joey rushes pregnant Rachel to hospital when she experiences pains. When Ross feels left out, Joey makes a gallant suggestion. Meanwhile, Chandler is surprised to discover what is behind the locked door of Monica's secret cupboard, and Phoebe gets the impression that Monica is enjoying one of her massages a little too much.
Monica prepares for a sexy Valentine's Day, but Chandler is too shell-shocked after accidentally viewing Rachel's birthing video. Meanwhile, Phoebe gives Joey the world's most cheerful dog.

A guilt-ridden Joey finally confesses his love for Rachel to the flabbergasted Ross, while Chandler becomes nervous when Phoebe's handsome new boyfriend Don shares numerous personality traits with Monica.
In an effort to restore normality to their friendship, Rachel tells Joey a big lie about her unborn child. Meanwhile, Phoebe's tea leaves reveal that she will soon encounter the man of her dreams.

Phoebe brings her irritatingly cheerful boyfriend to Mr and Mrs Geller's 35th anniversary party. Meanwhile, Ross is stunned when his parents ask him and the pregnant Rachel to feign marriage to avoid scandal.

The remaining members of Danny Ocean's gang regroup to jeopardise the nefarious plans of a businessman who double-crossed one of Danny's old friends. The team plans to ruin the opening of his glitzy Las Vegas casino and hotel by rigging the games and ensuring that every punter goes home with a jackpot.

Host Jimmy Carr and team captains Sean Lock and Jon Richardson are joined by Jack Dee, Claudia Winkleman, David O'Doherty and Josh Widdicombe as they thrash out the hot topics of the week by examining surveys, opinion polls and statistics.

Liff zerstört Kristophes Spielzeug, nimmt seinen Platz ein und Barry säubert die Puppe. Zudem erfahren Liff und Barry, dass ihre besten Tage vorbei sind. Daraufhin verlieren sie den Verstand. Wie wird dieser Konflikt enden?

Cricket und seine Familie ziehen vom Land in die Großstadt, was zuerst einen großen Kulturschock auslöst. Doch Cricket ist optimistisch und naiv, was ihn schnell neue Freunde finden lässt. Zusammen erleben sie viele Abenteuer in der großen Stadt.
Gramma legt sich mit Nick an, als er ihren besonderen Familien-Hockey-Ausflug stört.

pr.t: Mystery Lane - Ein Fall für Clever und Bro
pr.d: Ein Pudel wird eines Nachts in seinem Haus von einer Tentakelkreatur angegriffen.

Lilo nennt das neueste Experiment "Spitzel", weil es einen Lautsprecher eingebaut hat, der einem die Privatgespräche anderer mithören lässt. Als Nani herauskriegt, dass sie spioniert, bekommt Lilo Ärger. Trotzdem belauscht sie ein Gespräch zwischen Mertle und ihrer Mutter. Mertle redet von ihren Puppen, aber Lilo denkt, sie lästert über ihre Freundinnen und erzählt denen davon. Plötzlich hassen alle Mertle und spielen nur noch mit Lilo. Und Mertle versteht die Welt nicht mehr.

Die Jungs wollen beweisen, dass es das Wesen Chupacabra wirklich gibt. Aber Candace will die Jungs auffliegen lassen und durchkreuzt ihre Pläne. Ferb und die Bande feiern Isabellas Geburtstag, aber sie will nur mit Phineas etwas Zeit verbringen.

Als Muffin nicht aufhören kann, am Daumen zu lutschen, muss sie eine Halskrause tragen, um es sich abzugewöhnen. Die Halskrause stört sie jedoch sehr und sie kann nicht mehr mit Bluey und Bingo in ihrem Sandwichladen spielen.

Mama will dafür sorgen, dass Bluey und Bingo auf einem Familienausflug Spaß haben. Dad versucht, vor einem Konvoi grauer Nomaden zu bleiben, damit er nicht riskiert, in der Nähe der Toiletten sein Camp aufschlagen zu müssen.

Mama verbietet den Mädchen, ein bestimmtes Wort zu sagen, weil es kein Wort ist, das die Königin von England verwenden würde. Doch die Kinder kommen auf die Idee, zu versuchen, Mama trotzdem dazu zu bringen, es zu sagen.

Bluey will Papa helfen, den Bingo-Geburtstagskuchen zu backen, aber sie muss vorher noch ihre Spielsachen wegräumen. Nichts kann sie ermutigen, die Hausarbeit zu erledigen, bis Papa schließlich den Kuchen auf den Boden fallen lässt.

Auf einer Party versucht Bingo verzweifelt, den anderen ihre Künste im Handstand zu zeigen, während Nanna keinen Weg findet, sich nützlich zu machen. Beide fühlen sich ein wenig verloren, bis sie sich schließlich finden.

pr.t: Miraculous - Geschichten von Ladybug und Cat Noir
pr.d: Marinette ist überzeugt, dass Nora und ihr Kollege Twig heimlich Gefühle füreinander hegen. Doch beide sind offenbar viel zu schüchtern, um sich ihre Zuneigung zu gestehen, weshalb die Situation festgefahren zu sein scheint.

pr.t: Miraculous - Geschichten von Ladybug und Cat Noir
pr.d: Die Schüler Marinette und Adrien erhalten die Fähigkeit, sich in die Superhelden Ladybug und Cat Noir zu verwandeln und können dadurch das Glück und das Pech manipulieren. Sie wollen dem Bösewicht Hawk Moth das Handwerk legen.

Cricket und seine Familie ziehen vom Land in die Großstadt, was zuerst einen großen Kulturschock auslöst. Doch Cricket ist optimistisch und naiv, was ihn schnell neue Freunde finden lässt. Zusammen erleben sie viele Abenteuer in der großen Stadt.
Gloria verbindet ihr Arbeits- und Privatleben, indem sie ihre Freundinnen einstellt.

Haley und Alex stellen der Familie ihre sehr unterschiedlichen Lebenspartner vor: Während Haley mit einem Astrophysiker zusammen ist, hat sich Alex in einen Feuerwehrmann verliebt. Derweil sehen sich Jay und Gloria mit perfekten Eltern konfrontiert.

Als einer von Glorias ehemaligen Partnern auftaucht, fällt Jay dessen Ähnlichkeit zu Manny auf. Infolgedessen stellt er Javiers Vaterschaft infrage. Derweil zerbricht sich Phil den Kopf bezüglich des perfekten Geschenks für Claire zum Hochzeitstag.
Ted lernt im MacLaren's die äußerst attraktive Holly kennen. Die beiden tauschen ihre Handynummern aus. Barney und Marshall raten Ted jedoch, unbedingt die sogenannte "Dreitageregel" einzuhalten.

Ted bekommt den Auftrag, ein Restaurant in der Form eines Cowboyhuts zu entwerfen. Als er sich eine Pause gönnt, trifft er nach einer Verkettung von Zufällen auf der Straße plötzlich auf Stella, die er seit der Trennung nicht mehr gesehen hat.

Stellas Mann Tony hat ein schlechtes Gewissen, weil er Teds Beziehung mit Stella zerstört hat, und bietet Ted einen Job an. Doch dieser lehnt ab und bringt so Tonys Ehe ins Wanken. Barney versucht derweil, durch Flirten einem Strafzettel zu entgehen.

J.D.s Freundin Kylie hat ihn noch immer nicht bei sich einziehen lassen. Carla und Turk haben ihn vor die Tür gesetzt und nun wandert er einsam durch die Nacht. Inzwischen wird Dr. Cox von seinem alten Highschool-Freund Ron besucht.

Molly schaut für einen kurzen Besuch im Sacred Heart vorbei. Vor allem J.D. freut sich riesig über diese Überraschung. Denn da Kylie ihn noch immer nicht ans "Eingemachte" lässt, verfällt er der Idee, Molly zu verführen.

Carla sucht bei Elliot Unterschlupf, während J.D. und Turk auf Kneipentour gehen. Elliot versucht Carla aufzuheitern, aber es gelingt ihr nicht so recht. Cox überredet Dr. Kelso, sich auch mal selbst wieder um einen Patienten zu kümmern.

Tim bittet Harrys Sohn Dennis darum, einen zweiten Telefonanschluss in seinem Haus einzurichten. Während des Einbaus wird Dennis allerdings zu einem anderen Auftrag gerufen und so muss Tim die Arbeit zu Ende bringen.

Brad hat seine Führerscheinprüfung erfolgreich abgeschlossen und will sich Tims Wagen ausleihen. Jill, die darüber besorgt ist, wird auch gleich in ihren Zweifeln bestätigt, als Brad einen Unfall baut.
Tim steht vor einem neuen Rekord: Er hat bald mehr Heimwerkersendungen präsentiert als Bob Vila. Doch sein bevorstehender Triumph wird durch eine Schulterverletzung gefährdet.

Der jährliche Familienausflug zur Haushaltswarenausstellung in Cleveland steht bevor. Jill freut sich, mit den Kindern etwas unternehmen zu können und Tim moderiert von dort aus seine Sendung. Die Kinder haben jedoch dort andere Pläne.
Weil ihre Mutter während eines Shoppingtrips vom Verkäufer für ihre Schwester gehalten wird und deshalb abgelenkt ist, sammelt Barbara eine Menge Kleidung an, bevor es ans Bezahlen geht.

Howard finds that his new bike is difficult to conceal from Pearl. With a friend like Clegg, however, all his worries are multiplied.

Gordon Ramsay travels to Baltimore to try to turn around a restaurant that is suffering because its owner, Denise Whiting, has managed to alienate the surrounding community. When Denise opened Café Hon in 1992 it was a roaring success, but as a result of her unwavering business ambition the local community decided to boycott the restaurant, leaving Denise frustrated by falling sales.

Gordon Ramsay travels to South Philadelphia to try to turn around family-run restaurant Chiarella's, which is struggling to survive in an area full of thriving Italian establishments. That isn't the only problem facing owners Tommy and Dina Defino. Their marriage is on the verge of collapse.

When one of Vivian's brightest college students begins dating Will, her grades slide, threatening her scholarship.
As Christmas approaches, Lisa searches for a new religion after Mr Burns takes over her church and runs it like a corporation.

Homer becomes a good listener and a calming influence when his jaw is wired shut after he runs into a statue. However, Marge is disturbed by his new personality.

It's day two of the national finals, and the eight champions cook their fish courses. This year's challenge has been to produce dishes that are a lasting legacy to the New Elizabethan Age. They must showcase the transformation in British cuisine during the Queen's historic 64-year reign.

It's main course day, the one course every chef wants to cook at the banquet. The chefs' dishes will be judged by Matthew Fort, Prue Leith and Oliver Peyton along with guest judge John Williams MBE, executive chef of The Ritz.

It's the final day of the competition, and the last chance for the eight champions to get one of their dishes to the banquet for Queen Elizabeth II's Great Britons. Judges Matthew Fort, Prue Leith and Oliver Peyton will judge the dessert course and then decide on the banquet menu to be served at the Houses of Parliament. Joining them in the judging chamber is Grace Dent, restaurant critic, journalist and author.

The winning chefs arrive at the Palace of Westminster to cook for the Banquet of Great Britons. The chefs have been selected because their dishes showcase contemporary British cuisine and demonstrate the transformation in British food during the Queen's historic reign.

The three chefs meet their surprise veteran judge and cook their starters. A dish celebrating childhood summer memories takes on a complicated courgette dish and a technically tricky take on the cucumber sandwich.

The atmosphere in the kitchen gets even more intense as all the chefs take risks with their dishes. Mike Reid, executive chef at M Restaurants in London, shocks when he pairs his fish with some highly unusual flavours.

The kitchen is filled with smoke as the three chefs prepare their summer-themed mains. Selin Kiazim is in her element, preparing a feast inspired by the summer barbecues. Mike Reid uses wagyu beef. Tom Kemble uses juniper branches to smoke his meat.
All three chefs are feeling the pressure as they attempt their technical summer desserts. With only the two highest scorers going through to the regional final, who will be sent home?

The two remaining London and the South East chefs must cook their entire taste of summer menus again. They're hoping to impress the formidable panel of Oliver Peyton, Matthew Fort and restaurateur Andi Oliver.
The chefs have been challenged to create outstanding dishes that capture a 'taste of summer'. Their menus must reflect the tastes, smells and colours of everybody's favourite time of year.

It's the fish course and, with a seafood specialist in the kitchen, the competition is stepping up a gear. Tom is hoping he'll be able to elevate the humble mackerel to the standards required for the 🎾 [Tennis] Wimbledon banquet.

With a refined summer barbecue going up against a traditional Cornish speciality and a historic 🎾 [Tennis] Wimbledon related recipe, who will come out on top? Andy Clatworthy is using his passion for historical cooking to reinvent a dish.
All three chefs are honouring 🎾 [Tennis] Wimbledon and the British summer with their technically challenging strawberry desserts. Only the two highest scorers will go through to cook for the judges.
The two remaining chefs compete for a place in the national finals. To get there they'll have to impress the formidable panel of judges: Oliver Peyton, Matthew Fort and restaurateur Andi Oliver.

Tom Parker is eager to impress with a salad that includes 10 elements. Meanwhile, Paul Askew, hopes his traditional techniques will triumph over his younger competitors, and Ellis Barrie is taking a risk with a creative cucumber and oyster starter.

It is the fish course and the atmosphere in the kitchen gets even tenser as the three newcomers begin to understand the perfection and skill the veteran chef demands. Ellis Barrie attempts to create the flavour of a summer barbecue.

It is the main course and the pressure is intense in the kitchen. In the hope of impressing the veteran judge, Paul Askew is serving an extremely personal main course based on his mother's favourite food.

Dessert is the last chance for the chefs to secure a place cooking for the judges and the pressure in the kitchen is intense. Paul can't afford to make any mistakes and is pushing himself with a technically challenging baked Alaska.

The two remaining north-west chefs must cook their entire taste of summer menus again. The guest judge is Greg Rusedski, former British number one, who understands the high standards expected at 🎾 [Tennis] Wimbledon.

Returning banquet champion Tommy Banks takes on two ambitious newcomers, Danny Parker and Josh Overington. They start by finding out who is the surprise veteran judge and who will be marking their dishes.

The atmosphere in the kitchen gets even more heated, the three chefs are cooking their fish courses. Josh Overington creates a decadent dish inspired by the prestige of the 🎾 [Tennis] Wimbledon Championships.

The chefs are cooking their main courses and are all taking risks to try and win a place at the banquet. Danny Parker is trying to recreate the flavours of an American barbecue, but the veteran chef is dubious about one of his ingredients.
Dessert is the last chance for the chefs to secure a place cooking for the judges and the pressure in the kitchen is intense. All the chefs are using unusual ingredients in their desserts.

The two remaining chefs from the north-east must cook their entire taste of summer menus again. They're hoping to impress the formidable panel of judges Oliver Peyton, Matthew Fort, Andi Oliver, and guest Judy Murray.

It is the Scottish regional heats and returning chefs to the competition Michael Bremner and Ally McGrath battle ambitious newcomer Angela Malik for a place in the national finals. This time they are cooking their starters.

The atmosphere in the kitchen gets even more heated and the veteran chef is expecting perfection from the fish course. Ally McGrath creates an inventive dish based on his summer memories of rock pooling in the River Tweed.
Angela Malik is in her element cooking a tiffin box based on memories of summer picnics. Michael Bremner is taking a huge risk, and Ally is creating an inventive dish based on a summer barbecue.
Dessert is the last chance for the chefs to secure a place cooking for the judges and the pressure in the kitchen is intense. Angela Malik is cooking a technically challenging dessert.

The two Scottish chefs must cook their entire taste of summer menus again. They're hoping to impress the formidable panel of judges Oliver Peyton, Matthew Fort and Andi Oliver. They are joined by guest judge Gary Parsons.

Determined newcomers Paul Croasdale and Nick Brodie take on returning chef Phil Carmichael for a place in the national finals. It's Phil's third time in the competition and this year he's determined to make it to the banquet.

The pressure in the kitchen is high as the chefs prepare their fish courses. Paul Croasdale is trying to recreate the elegance of 🎾 [Tennis] Wimbledon with luxury ingredients such as king crab and scallops.

For the main course, all three chefs are cooking Welsh lamb in the hope of impressing the judge. Phil is taking a risk with barbecued lamb and in an attempt to elevate a humble barbecue to banquet level, he's serving it with many accompaniments.

It's the dessert course and the last chance for the chefs to secure a place cooking for the judges, so all three chefs are feeling the pressure. Phil Carmichael creates a tennis ball dessert that combines two British classics, Eton mess and trifle.

The two winning chefs from the Wales region must cook their entire taste of summer menus again. They're hoping to impress the formidable panel of judges and guest judge Dan Bloxham, 🎾 [Tennis] Wimbledon's Master of Ceremonies.

Pip Lacey's starter is a humorous take on the unpredictable British weather and features an unusual presentation. Ryan Simpson's dish represents an allotment complete with soil, while Nick Deverell-Smith's creation is a tribute to the precision cutting of 🎾 [Tennis] Wimbledon's grass.

With the chefs hoping to impress, they each take risks. Pip Lacey combines lobster with strawberry in a tribute to strawberries and cream. Ryan Simpson's also using lobster in his recreation of a BBQ and has invented a technique to create his chips.

Ryan Simpson hopes to elevate a ploughman's lunch into a gourmet affair, Pip Lacey pays tribute to an unusual 🎾 [Tennis] Wimbledon icon, while Nick Deverell-Smith looks to celebrate a meat which he thinks is underused, venison.

Dessert is the last chance for the chefs to secure a place cooking for the judges. Pip Lacey's pineapple dessert uses coriander. Nick Deverell-Smith also pays tribute to the pineapple, creating a dessert featuring a rice pudding made with couscous.

The two chefs who've made it through cook their four courses again. They must impress the formidable panel of judges Oliver Peyton, Matthew Fort, Andi Oliver and guest judge Jordanne Whiley, one of Britain's most successful wheelchair tennis players.

The chefs meet their surprise veteran judge and cook their starters. Eddie is hoping to do better than last year, Joery is hoping to impress with a tribute to Richard Krajicek, and Tommy is creating a warm salad.

Joery Castel is combining mackerel and cucumber, and Tommy Heaney hopes his Murray Mound is a fitting tribute to Andy Murray's love of sushi. Eddie Attwell is creating five different strawberry elements to accompany the scallops in his dish.

Beneath the quaint farmlands of Strathroy, Ontario, a disturbing history of fires, train wrecks, and serial killers casts intense paranormal energy over the charming small town and its residents.
Beneath Bellaire, Ohio's serene surface lies a history marked by bloodshed and tragedy. Bellaire sits directly above the crosshairs of a global paranormal energy grid known as a ley line.

Across three small towns in North America, three completely different people are tormented by child ghosts who are trapped in their homes. Haunting lullabies, dark figures, and tortured child spirits push these unsuspecting homeowners to the limit.

Around the world, mines, quarries and tunnels are often the site of unexplained events and ghostly encounters. Exploring how the electromagnetic properties of these mineral-rich areas may create the perfect conduits for the paranormal.

Honey's son's life is saved by a ghost, while Robert walks away from a deadly industrial accident when a ghost takes the hit for him.

Guernsey, the only British isle occupied by Nazi Germany during WWII, reveals unique wartime history.

pr.t: World War II: Saving the Reality
pr.d: Kenneth W Rendell's collection of World War II memorabilia features more than 6,000 original artefacts, including propaganda posters, French Resistance clothing, a Japanese admiral's uniform and a Sherman tank.
Carl Wark is a hill fort of unproven origin, but Bronze Age artefacts suggest a long occupation of the area. Tune in to see what the team can find.
The tale of the teenage Duke of Brittany and would-be King of England's suspicious demise which many believe was planned by his uncle King John.
The death of Robert Dudley's wife in 1560 caused a scandal - as the nobleman was Elizabeth I's alleged lover.

Bradley explores the Great Sphinx and the underground Serapeum with its precision-cut granite sarcophagi, questioning their purpose and links to the pyramid enigma. Travelling south, he visits the intricately designed Dendera Temple.
In Cheltenham, Britain's most Regency town, Professor Alice Roberts attends a period society ball, investigates social hierarchy and explores the Regency fondness for enemas.
In Belfast, the UK's most Victorian city, Alice Roberts visits the shipyards that built the Titanic, gets locked up in the Crumlin Road gaol and learns about 19th-century etiquette.

Andy embarks on a journey back to Scotland, exploring Rosslyn Chapel and its intriguing connection to the Holy Grail. He meets Billy Kirkwood at a cave believed to house a legendary beast and uncovers the story of Scotland's most infamous witch.

Professor Alice Roberts explores the English Civil War through the history of Oxford, the city at the heart of a battle between an autocratic king and his rebellious parliament. Oxford became the power base for Charles I and his royalist supporters.
Archaeological finds from Roman Britannia include 97 baby skeletons buried near the Thames, a town in rural Devon, and a Roman cult figure that remained buried beneath a fort for 1700 years.

Dr Alice Roberts looks at some excavations that offer a different perspective on the Vikings. She searches in the Outer Hebrides and Orkney for early Viking settlements. The Viking chief's citadel reveals information about their way of life.
Discovering the truth of the unsolved murder of Josslyn Hay, 22nd Earl of Erroll, who was shot in Kenya in 1941, and why the only suspect was acquitted.

In 12th-century Ireland, provincial kings vie for supremacy. When two of these power players drive a rival into exile, he seeks help from Henry II, the Anglo-Norman king of England. Henry's vassal Strongbow and other Norman allies then invade Ireland with frightening power.

Alice visits Canterbury for the story of Plantagenet England. Canterbury is steeped in history and the era of the Plantagenets - the strong house that held the English throne from 1154 until 1485 - saw the most dramatic episodes in the city's story.
Alice Roberts explores the story of Stewart Britain by visiting Stirling, the home of the Scottish royals who eventually took the English throne in 1603 and created Great Britain.

Andy explores the origins of modern witches, attends a vampire masquerade with Dracula and investigates a fairy hoax, revealing myth versus reality. He also teams up with experts to explore the legendary werewolves of the Yorkshire Wolds.
Andy visits Hereford Cathedral to discover the cider tax's role in the American Civil War, while Jayne explores local legends, including a bell stealing mermaid and a girl's love for her pet dragon.

Finds include the lost WWI training trenches on Salisbury Plain, Britain's first 'double henge', discovered just down the road from Stonehenge, where the evidence suggests our ancestors feasted and made sacred offerings as part of a visit to the ritualistic Stonehenge landscape, and luxury foreign goods discovered at Tintagel, the legendary childhood home of King Arthur.
The team is in the north of Britain where they uncover evidence of the first Roman siege in Britain, Scottish man-made islands and a famous monastery.

Dan Jones explores the history of Cardiff Castle over more than 2,000 years and reveals how it became transformed from a strategically important Roman and Norman stronghold to a lavish fairy-tale Victorian home.

Edinburgh's handsome hilltop bastion is Scotland's most popular paid tourist attraction. With a slew of sieges to its name, it is no surprise that the site boasts some formidable defences, and Dan puts one heavy-duty cannon through its paces.

Professor Alice Roberts tells the story of Edwardian Britain by visiting Cardiff, which grew rich selling the coal that powered the Empire. Alice hears the stories of the Edwardian miners and their backbreaking and often dangerous work.

Professor Alice Roberts explores the English Civil War through the history of Oxford, the city at the heart of a battle between an autocratic king and his rebellious parliament. Oxford became the power base for Charles I and his royalist supporters.

The death of the Queen's uncle, Prince George, Duke of Kent, in a plane crash in 1942 has never been fully explained. The mysterious circumstances surrounding the crash has led to accusations that the Prince has been airbrushed from history.
King Ludwig of Bavaria's unstable behaviour saw him deposed from the throne in 1886. Days later, he was found dead. Was it suicide or murder?
The final words of a lifelong gold hunter send Adam, Kru and Daryl Friesen through an icy gauntlet high above Pitt Lake.
An old map connected to testimony from an 1891 eyewitness account of Slumach's hanging sheds light on the legend.

pr.t: Unser Traum vom Schloss: Tipps und Tricks
pr.d: Die Strawbridges planen den Geburtstag von Tochter Dorothy auf dem Schloss. Ihre Feier soll rund um die neue Meerjungfrauenhütte ausgerichtet werden. Außerdem helfen Angel und Dick einem Pärchen bei dem Ausbau ihres alten Wohnwagens.

Dick und Angel laden zu ihrem traditionellen Weihnachtsfest für alle Helfer ein und bereiten aufwändige Menüs sowie liebevoll gestaltete Geschenke vor. Ein überraschender winterlicher Höhepunkt rundet das Jahr stimmungsvoll ab.

Tamara renoviert eine wunderschöne Villa im Neu-Tudorstil in einer exklusiven Nachbarschaft, die sie zu einem guten Preis ergattern konnte. Im ersten Renovierungsabschnitt soll das Erdgeschoss komplett umgestaltet werden.

Tamara ist mit der Renovierung einer Ranch am See beschäftigt und gestaltet das Schlafzimmer. Dazu soll es aber auch ein anliegendes Ankleidezimmer geben und ein direkter Zugang zu einem neuen Bad geben. Anschließend geht es im Garten weiter.

Für das Obergeschoss der Villa im Neu-Tudorstil plant Nicole ein großes Elternschlafzimmer mit Bad und schönem Balkon. Doch das absolute Highlight des Hauses soll der große, sonnige Garten werden. Doch die Renovierung kommt nicht problemlos.

Bei der Renovierung einer einstöckigen Ranch stößt Tamara auf ihre bisher größte Herausforderung. Sie will das ehemalige Masterschlafzimmer in eine atemberaubende und offene Küche verwandeln, doch stößt sie dabei auf Probleme mit ihrem Vater.

Am Abend bringt Elizabeth die Ernte auf den Tisch und bereitet ein typisches Santa Maria Style Tri-Tip mit einer fruchtigen Blackberry-Apple Galette zu. So verbindet sich das harte Ranchleben mit Genussmomenten im Familienkreis.

Auf der Ranch läutet Elizabeth den Frühling mit der Ernte von frischem Honig ein. Sie nutzt ihn für einen duftenden Zitronen-Honig-Kuchen und zeigt, wie vielseitig die süße Zutat in der Küche ist. Sie bereitet Zitronen-Buttermilch-Fried-Chicken zu.

Der Tag auf der Ranch beginnt für Elizabeth mit einem Hummingbird Breakfast Cake, der die Cowboys für die Arbeit mit dem Vieh stärkt. Danach geht es hinaus aufs Feld, wo das Team die Herde zusammentreibt. Zum Abschluss gibt es Brisket-Sandwiches.

Elizabeth erwartet Besuch von ihrer Cousine Roz und deren Familie und bereitet dafür ein festliches Barbecue vor. Neben frischem Focaccia mit Kräutern und essbaren Blüten serviert sie Schweinerippchen, die langsam in Apfelwein gegart werden.

Elizabeth und Austin gönnen sich eine kleine Auszeit. Nach einem Angelausflug an der kalifornischen Küste serviert Elizabeth frischen Fisch mit Zitronen-Dill-Soße, Safranreis und Ricotta-Keksen. Es ist ein Abend, der Arbeit, Liebe und Genuss vereint.

Die Erntezeit auf der Ranch ist süß: Elizabeth verarbeitet erntefrische Erdbeeren zu Marmelade und feinem Shortcake mit Ingwersahne. Bei einem gemütlichen Abend am Feuer kommt die Familie zusammen, um die Früchte des Sommers zu genießen.

Bevor sie eine Familie gründen, möchten Jamey und Lucas noch eine Weile in Europa leben. Ihnen schwebt ein Haus mit großem Innen- und Außenbereich in Amsterdam vor, aber die beliebte Grachtenstadt hält nur kleine Häuser für viel Geld bereit.

Mit der Sehnsucht nach mehr Sonne und einem gesünderen Lebensstil möchte ein Paar nach Tulum, Mexiko, ziehen. Doch während sie auch genügend Platz für die erwachsenen Kinder haben möchte, reicht ihm ein Zuhause für zwei Personen.

Obwohl Debbie in Manhattan als Künstlerin etabliert ist, möchte sie mit ihren Kindern nach Lissabon ziehen. Dort angekommen fängt sie aber an, alles mit dem Big Apple zu vergleichen und hängt ihrem einstigen extravaganten Leben nach.

Inspiriert von einer Rucksackreise in ihrer Jugend, möchten Mike und Wendy ihren sechs Töchtern die italienische Kultur mit einem Umzug nach Parma näherbringen. Allerdings bereitet das Budget dem Umzug der Großfamilie Probleme.

Die Schriftstellerinnen Casie und Casey sind Weltenbummlerinnen und möchten sich nun in der vietnamesischen Küstenstadt Da Nang niederlassen. Allerdings möchte Casie in die Innenstadt, während Casey ein Haus am Strand vorschwebt.
Diese Sendung wirbt für verschiedene Produkte, die man sich bequem nach Hause schicken lassen kann.

Jack und Sharon aus Buffalo, New York, gewinnen sieben Millionen Dollar. Einer ihrer Söhne legt sich gleich eine Junggesellenbude zu. Nun suchen auch die Eltern selbst nach ihrem Traumhaus, das eine große Küche und eine Männerhöhle bieten soll.

Während sie in der Calgary Central Library sind, begeben sich die Brüder mit einer bei den Fans beliebten Folge auf eine Reise in die Vergangenheit, in der sie einer Familie zu Hilfe kommen, deren Mietwohnungen zu groß geworden sind.
George und Jenn möchten näher an Familie und Freunde ziehen, können sich aber nicht einig werden.

Candice und Brian fliehen vor dem kalten Winter in Denver, Colorado. Sie ziehen nach Cocoa Beach, Florida. Der Broker Andy Barclay soll ihnen helfen, ein neues Zuhause zu finden. Um etwas zu sparen, wollen Brian und Candice auch selbst Hand anlegen.

Virginia und Stephanie haben ein Budget von 200.000 Dollar und suchen nach einem Schnäppchen am 🏌️ [Golf] Golf von Mexiko. Die Renovierung muss inklusive sein. Das Anwesen soll unbedingt eine Veranda haben und im Cottage-Stil gebaut sein.

Ein Paar will mit seinen drei Kindern in den zwei Stunden von Seattle entfernten Ort Westport ziehen, der unter Meeresfrüchteliebhabern und Surfern bekannt ist. Amy und Randy beginnen mit den Renovierungen, werden dabei aber mehrmals überrascht.

Tamara und ihr Vater helfen einer frisch gebackenen Witwe, die gerne für ihre Familie kocht, bei der Gestaltung ihrer Traumküche. Tamara verwandelt eine kleine Kombüse in eine riesige Traumküche, die sich perfekt für große Familienfeiern eignet.

Tamara und ihr Team verwandeln ein charmantes Tudorhaus aus dem Jahr 1927 in ein absolutes Meisterwerk, das komplett mit einer neuen, komfortableren, funktionelleren und farbenfroheren Küche und einem erweiterten Hauptbad ausgestattet wird.

Eine veraltete Ranch aus den 60er-Jahren muss dringend renoviert werden, und so tut sich Tamara mit einem Investor zusammen, um das Anwesen von einem tristen in ein wunderschönes Haus zu verwandeln. Dabei setzen sie ihre gesamten Fähigkeiten ein.

Tänzerin Karen kämpft mit einem Bungalow aus den 70er-Jahren, der von Erinnerungen an ihre verstorbenen Angehörigen geprägt ist. Um Platz für eine positive Zukunft zu schaffen, muss sie sich von vielen Gegenständen trennen.

Die Einrichtungsexpertin Kanoa Lloyd und ihr Team zeigen, wie man Ordnung in den Alltag bringt. Gemeinsam mit dem Schreiner Sean Brown und der Organisationsexpertin Natalie Jane entrümpeln sie chaotische Häuser in Neuseeland.

Silvanas Unordnung führt zu Konflikten in ihrem Haushalt und Peter drängt sie dazu, die Vergangenheit loszulassen, Cherie schafft einen Raum für Familientreffen und Angie bastelt einen Hula-Hoop-Reifen, um Erinnerungen zur Schau zu stellen.

Mit drei Kindern und wichtigen Jobs im Gesundheitswesen ist das Haus von Nina und Dom voller Unordnung. Peter packt die 381 Kisten voller Sachen an, während Cherie die Küche auseinanderreißt, um einen großen, offenen Raum zu schaffen.

Nick begibt sich nach Farnborough in Hampshire, wo es für ein Paar mit drei Kindern, die in einem überfüllten Reihenhaus mit drei Schlafzimmern leben, um alles geht. Unter der Leitung des Designers Gordon arbeitet Nicks Team an einer Neugestaltung.

Nick begibt sich an die Themse, wo eine alleinerziehende Mutter und ihre drei Kinder in Unordnung versinken und auf engstem Raum in einem Hausboot leben. Da Mutter Anna ein Unternehmen führt, hat sie keine Zeit, das Durcheinander aufzuräumen.

Die Holmes-Familie unterstützt ihren Freund Frank, der wegen gesundheitlicher Probleme mit seiner Renovierung kämpft. Währenddessen bringt Mike die Farbwahl eines Bungalows an seine Grenzen, als er die kreativen Designentscheidungen hinterfragt.
Martin, Lucy and Dion visit a grand five-bedroom period house in Folkestone in Kent, a two-bedroom flat in London's Leytonstone and a two-bedroom mid-terrace in Fenton in Stoke-on-Trent.

A studio flat in a former 1960s office block which is grade two listed in London's Elephant and Castle, a terraced house in Pontygwaith in South Wales and a flat in Cradley Heath near Birmingham are all sold under the hammer.
A house with no floor in Edgbaston in Birmingham, a detached house on several levels in Oldham and a former garage complex ripe for development in Forest Hill in London are all sold under the hammer.
A converted 16th-century chapel in Matlock in Derbyshire, a two-bedroom flat in Whetstone in London and a water-damaged house in Wishaw in Scotland are all sold under the hammer.

A two-bed semi in Meir in Stoke-on-Trent is given a country house look, a flat in London's Willesden Green also gets the wow factor, and a semi in Dudley in the West Midlands loses its 1980s look to be brought into the 21st century.
Terraced houses in Gravesend in Kent and Shipley in Derbyshire are given a new lease of life while former church premises in Harrow Weald in Middlesex are given a new use for the community.

Martin, Lucy and Dion meet property developers who have all bought at auction and hope to make a profit on their investments. Today a landscape gardener tackles a terrace in Ilkeston in Derby, two friends take on a four-storey house in Sittingbourne in Kent while another couple of friends' first venture together is a studio flat in South Norwood in London.
The trio look at a family home in Kent, a former bar in Llanelli in Wales and a terrace in Croydon, all sold at auction. Will any of the developers make a return on their investments?

A three-bedroom semi in Crewe, a top-floor flat in London and a terraced house in Oldham are sold under the hammer. All the owners are happy with the prices they paid, but will any of them be able to turn a profit at the end of the projects?

While developers in Croydon in Surrey and Donnington in Shropshire wrestle with whether to lose a bedroom each for a better placed kitchen or bathroom, two friends in Derby consider creating two more in their six-bedroom house.

Two brothers buy a rundown cottage in Probus in Cornwall, a father buys a flat in Mitcham in Surrey as a long-term investment for his young daughter and a seasoned property developer buys a house in Tunstall in Stoke-on-Trent for her daughter.

Dion is in Plaistow in London looking around a three-bedroom semi, Lucy is checking out a small piece of land in Crayford in Kent, and Martin meets a father and son who have bought a small house with a big garden in Wheelock in Cheshire.
A former miner's cottage in Aberaman in South Wales and semis in Adderley Green in Stoke and Streatham in South London are all sold under the hammer.
Martin, Lucy and Dion look around auction buys in Birmingham, Oldham and Gravesend and discover what the new owners plan to do with their investments.
Martin Roberts, Lucy Alexander and Dion Dublin are in Stoke, Croydon in London and Warrington hearing tales from the auction rooms.

A former doctor's surgery in need of TLC is converted into a family home in Houghton-le-Spring. Also, a flat in a 1930s block of flats in Edgware and a detached house in a woodland garden in Ashford in Kent are also given makeovers.

Three developers have very different reasons for making their investments: there's a family home in Consett in County Durham, a rental investment in Derby and an auction buy in Beckenham in London which will be used to run a new business, which the owner hopes will give him more time with his family.

Dion looks round a large Victorian terrace in Plumstead, Martin is in Mickleover in Derby hearing a father and daughter's plans for a flat and Lucy discovers what happened to a plot of land she saw five and a half years ago.

Martin looks round a bungalow in a stunning setting in the Lake District while Dion has a look at a flat close to Nottingham city centre. Lucy meets a woman who mistakenly thought she was buying a piece of land in Folkestone in Kent.
Lucy looks at a flat in Kilburn in London with one of the worst cases of damp she has ever seen, while Martin and Dion are in the Midlands looking round semis with potential.
A flat with huge potential in London's Earlsfield, and terraced houses in Wombourne near Wolverhampton and Ynyswen near Treorchy in Wales are all sold under the hammer.

Martin is impressed with the potential of two shops and three flats in Tonypandy in Wales while Dion looks round a two-bedroom maisonette in Dawley and Lucy meets a first-time developer with ambitious plans for an end terrace in London's Forest Gate.

Focuses on criminals who have been brought to justice for their crimes, only to be released to commit further atrocious acts. Includes interviews with relatives of the victims, and explores the issue of legal loopholes.

Examining the fatal stabbing of 22-year-old motorist Stephen Cameron during an altercation on the M25 in 1996.

Paramedic Paul Novak kills his wife Catherine, then sets fire to the house in a bid to make it look like an accidental death.

Mass accommodation sites are central to the government's plan to end the use of asylum hotels. This undercover investigation goes inside Crowborough, a former military training camp now housing asylum seekers. Filming covertly, the programme investigates conditions inside the site, finding how systemically poor welfare checks are having serious consequences. The film also examines the local community's response to asylum seekers being housed in the town, including a network of surveillance set up by local groups to monitor the camp's residents whenever they leave the site. It also looks at instances of intimidation towards people helping the new arrivals.

pr.t: Anwälte der Toten - Die schlimmsten Serienkiller der Welt
pr.d: Gary Ridgway, alias der Green-River-Killer, kam fast zwanzig Jahre mit den Morden an mindestens 49 Frauen davon. Erst im Jahr 2001 konnte er gefasst und verurteilt werden. Er tötete vor allem junge Frauen, Ausreißerinnen und Prostituierte.

Die Satelliten fangen Fotos von eigenartigen Hügeln in England ein. Als Archäologen dorthin reisen, stoßen sie auf eines der blutigsten Kapitel der Geschichte des Landes. In China werden kreisrunde Objekte in den Bergen entdeckt.

Der Archäologe Mark Horton entdeckt zwei große Risse in der irischen Landschaft. Bei seinen Untersuchungen stößt er auf eine Höhle, die ein mythisches Geheimnis in sich trägt. Demgegenüber zeigen historische Luftaufnahmen einen riesigen chinesischen See, der zu einer Pfütze geschrumpft ist. Doch was ist die Ursache? In der Doku gehen Experten diesen und weiteren Phänomenen genauer auf den Grund.

Auf Luftbildern sind die Überreste einer antiken Kirche zu erkennen, die sich auf dem Grund eines türkischen Sees befindet. Es handelt sich um ein Bauwerk aus den Anfängen des Christentums. Jedoch offenbart die Kirche eine heidnische Vergangenheit. Zudem taucht im Südpazifik eine Insel aus dem Nichts auf. Wissenschaftler entdecken Relikte, die aus den Tiefen der Erde ausgestoßen wurden. Weitere rätselhafte Phänomene werden ebenfalls enttarnt.

Peppa and Rebecca Rabbit pretend to be babies to get Mummy Rabbit's attention. Mummy Rabbit plays along until they admit they are not really babies!
Peppa is on a play date with Candy Cat at Mr Cat's Café. Candy shows Mr Cat the drawings they've done of everyone, and he hangs them up for everyone to see.
On a cold day, Daddy Pig suggests they build a den until Mummy Pig has finished work. After a hard day's work, the cushion den is a perfect place to watch TV together!
Auntie, Uncle Pig, and cousin Chloe are coming for dinner and Peppa is allowed to join too! Peppa is very proud of staying up late; she even stayed up later than the Daddies!
Lucy's dad is digging up the meadow and the Little Kingdom is in danger.
Barnaby Elf's uncle, Redbeard the Elf Pirate, comes to visit the Little Kingdom, but he has lost his treasure. Everyone must help Redbeard track down the treasure.
A new student, Gerald the giraffe, joins the playgroup where Peppa and her friends go. However, when he tries to fit in, he finds it difficult to play hide-and-seek because he is so tall.
Miss Rabbit takes Peppa and the family to Granny and Grandpa Pig's house to drop off their shopping, but that's not the last trip of the day for her.
When Peppa's bike gets a flat tyre that needs mending, Daddy Pig suggests they ride imaginary bikes. Peppa and her friends have fun riding their imaginary bikes and jumping in pretend muddy puddles.

Daddy Pig takes Peppa and George to school on their scooters. When he decides that it would be quicker to ride back, he discovers that riding scooters is great fun. Mummy Pig thinks that they are fun too and they both ride the scooters.
Mr Meerkat shows the children a huge wall that needs painting. They create a fantastic mural using lots of different techniques: brushes, sponges, buggy ropes and even a paint cannon!
It's the day of the duck race! When Miss Rabbit gives the sign, everyone drops their ducks in the river at the first bridge - whose will make it to the second bridge first?

At the gym, Madame Gazelle is teaching the children about martial arts. Along with Mr. Bull, the children learn how to fall safely, balance and even how to throw punches in the right stance. Mr. Bull gives them their white belts.

Dr Hamster has brought a giant ant farm and opens the ant farm's lid to show how they got in. Nobody noticed they escaped and starting moving things in the classroom! The children place food around to lead the ants safely back.
Grampy Rabbit gives Peppa and her friends a tour of an exercise park. Since the machines are only for grownups, the kids do funny exercises instead.
After seeing an advert for the London Marathon, Daddy Pig applies to take part to show the kids what grit and determination really looks like!
When a last-minute hitch puts a stop to the big kazoo concert, Thomas and his friends decide to hold a pizza picnic for everyone instead.
We ask who is stinking up the swamp. We find out who is behind the haunting voice in the forest!
Windsor Gardens has two new heroes, Jonathan is hailed a hero after saving a rare gnome.
Judy finds her inner hero on the Rangers Camping trip as they need to shelter from the weather; Paddington befriends a speedy snail with a heroic future ahead, but also looks so sad.
Paddington and Robot Paddington enjoy being heroes, Paddington discovers how to be calm.

After Peppa and family visit a tourist spot with her new friend Birgit Bear, the caravan unhooks from the car. The bear family stops it just in time, and they finish the day jumping muddy puddles at the caravan park.
At Chloe's birthday party, the children and grownups struggle to finish the inflatable obstacle course to reach the prize.
Miss Rabbit arrives with the broken Party Bus; this is a job for Grampy Rabbit.
Peppa is playing with Freddy Fox at his home, in a flat above the shops. Peggy and Pandora Panda and Candy Cat live there too, and help show Peppa around.
Peppa and family help make a garden on the roof of the flats. Mr Bull assists with a big truck and crane. There is even a little something for Mrs Duck.
Peppa is playing with Candy Cat when Emily Elephant's Granny moves out of the flat. When the new neighbours arrive, Peppa recognises her holiday friend Rohan Rhino.
Peppa and all her friends are having a sleep-over, with different friends in each of the four different flats in the high street. They decide to play hide and seek across all the rooms.
The children must walk to school in a walking bus. Miss Rabbit wears a high visibility jacket, leading Peppa and friends in a bus formation.
The Wingnuts get a new pet ostrich, but it gets lost on the trip home.
When an ancient relic goes missing from Carlos' archaeological dig, Tracker and Skye must find the creature that may have taken it.

The Browns meet Shantee the lighthouse keeper when they arrive at the beach for their holiday. Paddington, Jonathan, and Judy become trainee lifeguards and end up rescuing Mr Brown with Taylor the lifeguard's help.

Something is making the strange noises in the cave. Jonathan thinks it's a mermaid, but Paddington isn't so sure. Judy wants to find a fossil on the beach, but everyone else seems to be getting lucky except her. Paddington tries to help.
PAW Patrol is a CG action-adventure preschool series starring a pack of six heroic puppies led by a tech-savvy 10-year-old boy named Ryder.
Peppa and her friends from playgroup visit a science museum, where they learn all sorts of things.
George, Peppa and Mummy Pig head off to Miss Rabbit's clothes shop to get George some brand-new clothes. After trying on lots of new exciting outfits George finds an outfit that suits him just right!

Mummy Sheep gets the news that she has got a new job far away, leaving Suzy and Peppa to wonder how they're going to carry on being best friends; Peppa gives Suzy some presents to remember her by, before a surprising change for Mummy Sheep changes everything.

It is raining, and Grandpa Rabbit has built a rocket pack. As he demonstrates it to Peppa and George, he inadvertently ends up atop a snowy mountain. Miss Hare attempts to rescue him but becomes stranded on the mountaintop as well.

In this special episode, Speed Meister sabotages a speeding train, accidentally sending it towards a huge mountain! Rubble and Crew introduce their new demolition vehicles to smash through the mountain and build a tunnel to save the day!

Farmer Al's new machine, the Garboni, goes haywire, and it's up to Ryder and the Paw Patrol to stop it before it gives them the slip. The Paw Patrol have to catch a trouble-making sleepy porcupine and bring it back to the woods.
Tim tries to find a new rocket that's perfect for him.
When Terri and Tommy get locked in the Garden Dome, they must put their differences aside and try to escape.
Join Tim Rex, brother Tommy, sister Tia, and Triceratops bestie Kai as they tackle kid-shaped problems with dino-sized solutions! Tim, Tommy, Tia and Dad get stuck on a remote asteroid.
Gabby is the mechanic all the Monster Machines in town count on to fix them up. But when Crusher steals all her tools, Gabby needs Blaze's help to get them back.
Gabby and friends go all out for an extra special holiday, throwing a "paw-tastic" party, complete with homemade decorations and dessert.
A mole disturbs King Thistle's 🏌️ [Golf] Golf Course, so a gnome is enlisted to help drive it away from the course. Soon though, the gnome is turning the King's golf course into a crazy golf course.
The children are at the Elf Farm, but to learn where milk comes from they must visit a big farm, to find cows. The children travel to Lucy Big's farm, where she shows them all the animals.
Peppa and her friends are playing in their clubhouse, which has a fold-down counter at the front. The children pretend to run a little shop for the parents to buy things from.

At the playground, Pedro and Penny's glasses fall off; both think that their glasses are broken, as they cannot see very well; Madame Gazelle shows Pedro and Penny different types of objects with lenses.
Peppa and her family are on a caravan adventure; the first stop is the biggest potato in the world; when it starts to get too foggy, they park up for a rest before another busy day.
Features the grown-up's singing competition where the kids are the judges.
Peppa and her family hire a canoe from Miss Rabbit. They imagine they are in a jungle and then unexpectedly bump into Mrs Crocodile. Later on, Mr Lion invites them to have a picnic.
Peppa and George go behind the scenes to find out how TV is made when Miss Rabbit shows them around the set of Super Potato's TV show.
The playgroup visits a nature reserve, specialising in tiny insects, bugs, and butterflies. So Pedro brings along his pet stick insect.
Madame Gazelle tells the children all about wind power, then Mr Bull makes a lovely cup of tea made using the energy source.
Gargamel needs someone to watch over the Smurfs he's captured. Papa Smurf loses his memory and starts acting like a child.

The Goodways drift out to sea on a swan-shaped float and need rescue from a flock of real swans aiming to protect the giant inflatable; Mayor Humdinger steals Katie's Portable Pet Wash and ends up causing bubble trouble all over town.

Bears are asleep all over town! The PAW Patrol must work quietly to save the bears and return them to their cave. With the farmers out of town, Mayor Goodway calls the PAW Patrol to wrangle the animals and control the chaos on the farmerless farm.

Bibi goes live, but when she's not getting enough likes, Twister steps in to help, and is almost unmasked. Gran Gran's convinced that Chahuta won't impress a food critic, so tries to change the recipes.
Wandy gets a cold and is taken ill; Holly is given a replacement wand. This new wand can do lots of things that Wandy can't, and soon becomes the favourite.
Ben Elf and his parents are going on holiday in the elf truck but Gaston the Ladybird has swallowed the car keys.
Things are going missing all over the Little Kingdom - Holly has lost her wand and Ben has lost his horn! Soon they realise that ants are stealing their things.
Holly spends the day with King Thistle on his royal duties. King Thistle must launch an elf boat, judge a fairy fruit competition and make a speech at the festival.
Tim and Kai try to give Parky the best day ever.
Tim attempts to distract Tia whilst Tusky is being washed in the machine.
Tim, Tia and Tommy try to convince Mum and Dad to let them have a pet.
Cove beach is covered in a swarm of starfish! But everything is not as it seems! Why have they only got four arms, and why are they plastic?
Stan finds a special star stone which Grandad believes will bring him luck - and it does! But when Stan loses his star stone, will his luck change?
Annette blames herself for Emilios's hurt wing. Clarion becomes a superhero.

Doctor Hamster comes to school to talk about butterflies. Doctor Hamster shows the children some colourful caterpillars and all the children draw pictures of caterpillars. One caterpillar forms a chrysalis that opens to reveal a pretty butterfly. The children paint butterfly wings and dance the life cycle of a butterfly.

Peppa and her family are going for a drive. Suddenly their car breaks down, and it has to go to Granddad Dog's garage to be fixed. While their car is fixed, they borrow a shiny new, blue car from Granddad Dog.
Mummy Elephant invites Peppa and Daddy Pig to perform magic at Emily's birthday party. Peppa shows her friends how the magic trick works.
Peppa and George visit Granny and Grandpa Pig. Grandpa builds a special hiding hut to watch birds in so they can all go owl-spotting.

Lights, camera, CatRat; Gabby and the gang help turn a fairytale into a movie and get crafty with costumes, props and sound effects.
Peppa and her family go bowling at the Peppatown Bowling Alley.
George and Peppa spend the day playing golf with Grandpa Pig, but they are much more interested in the colourful mini-golf course next door.

Mummy Pig takes Peppa to the doctors for her yearly health check-up with Dr Polar Bear, who checks her height, weight, ears, mouth and heartbeat and listens to Mummy tell him all about the changes Peppa has gone through.

Peppa and George visit Granny and Grandpa's while Granny hosts a re-enactment of the 1960s with her friends.

The Elf Factory is deep down in the roots of The Great Elf Tree. It is almost Christmastime and the elves are busy making toys for the holidays. Some magic saves the day when there is a problem.

After getting through a rough night's sleep and finding out his beach day gets cancelled due to the rain, Thomas winds up in the grumpiest of moods.
